messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH SEV - OspreyBank (VPC/dedicated) - repeated model-variant evictions causing fallback to hosted safe-variant. Impact: intermittent 503s and increased latency for inference requests routed through their dedicated pool. Paging on-call SRE. :ambulance:
Maya: on it. seeing a stream of eviction events in the dedicated pool for tenant ospreybank-prod. autoscaler is killing pods due to OOMs on sequence-length spikes.
Owen: Ack. I’m grabbing logs + recent kernel OOM traces. Maya do we have a temporary mitigation to keep customer traffic from hitting the unstable nodes?
Maya: two immediate options: 1) pin the tenant routing to the safe-variant model (lower memory) in the routing policy, or 2) change tenant to route to their reserved spare nodes in another AZ (if available). Pinning is fastest.
Lina: tagging here for customer comms. OspreyBank is in a compliance window; they require us to avoid sending data to hosted multi-tenant models unless explicitly approved. If we fallback to hosted safe-variant that's a compliance flag for them. Need to coordinate before we flip anything customer-facing.
Darius: underlined — safety/consent constraint. We can do an intra-VPC override to route to a quantized safe-variant that lives in their VPC (we have one: `ospreybank/safe-quant-v1`). It’s lower perf but stays within their isolation.
Samir: quick status: autoscaler is thrashing due to large-batch jobs that spiked token usage about 3m ago. Node memory pressure at 92%. Evictions correlate with a specific k8s taint being applied by the eviction-controller.
Elliot: Customer-impact summary from Support: ~2.3% of requests returning 503s over the last 12 mins, spike in tail latency to ~9s. No evidence of data leakage, but increased error rates are triggering customer alerts.
Maya: proposed live mitigation: apply a tenant-level `model_pin` for ospreybank-prod to `ospreybank/safe-quant-v1` (VPC variant) via the private control plane API. This keeps traffic in their VPC and avoids hosted fallback. After pin, scale down batch sizes for the tenant to reduce memory pressure.
Owen: agree. Steps I'd run now (execute once we have Lina/customer sign-off):
```bash
# pin tenant routing to VPC-safe-variant
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/tenants/ospreybank/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model_pin":"ospreybank/safe-quant-v1","pin_reason":"eviction-mitigation-3650001234","force":true}'

# then reduce batch size to limit memory
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/tenants/ospreybank/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"batching":{"max_tokens":256,"concurrency":8}}'
```
Samir: if we pin, we must also patch the autoscaler rule so it won't overreact to short-lived spikes. I'll prepare a temporary policy: `eviction_tolerance: 3m` for the pool.
Lina: I'll reach out to OspreyBank (primary: alice@ospreybank.com, security: sec@) right now. They asked to stay in-VPC only — so confirm that we will not route to hosted variants. Please hold on any hosted fallback changes until I get approval.
Darius: note: there is a small model-behavior delta between regular and quant variant. We should enable a light canary header so we can correlate quality regressions: `x-rw-canary=osprey-evict-1` and collect eval samples to send to their SRE.
Maya: can we do the pin in read-only mode first (i.e., apply but do not route traffic) to validate config? We don't have a two-step pin API but we can push the config and use the `route_override=false` flag, then flip to true after checks.
Owen: I'll stand by to execute once Lina confirms customer permission. Meanwhile I'm attaching recent kube logs that show OOM kill stack and the continuous batch job IDs.
(attachment): ```
[OOM] pod/generator-7c4b Killed process 3245 (python) total-vm:24G anon-rss:18G
batch_job_id: batch-2026-03-15-12:04
tail: Traceback (most recent call last): ... MemoryError
```
Lina: OspreyBank (Alice) confirmed by DM: they prefer in-VPC safe-variant. Approve immediate pin and batching reduction. They also want an ETA for full remediation and post-incident report.
Maya: executing the pinned route now. Will post command output. :white_check_mark:
(automation): config update accepted: model_pin=ospreybank/safe-quant-v1; batching updated. change_id=cfg-98765
Samir: autoscaler policy patched: `eviction_tolerance: 3m` on ospreybank-dedicated-pool.
Elliot: Support sees error rate drop to 0.4% in the last 3 mins and tail latency down to ~2.2s. Customer alerts cleared on their side.
Darius: creating a short-lived rollback plan: if errors increase >1% for 5m, auto-unpin and route to dedicated-fallback-standby (which is their reserved warm nodes) — but need to ensure this does not violate the customer's in-VPC requirement. We'll keep the auto-unpin off for now.
Maya: adding runbook link for on-call docs and follow-up: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-eviction-mitigation. Also will schedule a full postmortem and capacity tune with infra/research.
Owen: handing off to morning oncall (Samir) at shift change in 40m. Samir you have ownership for follow-up and remediation tracking.
Samir: got it. I'll follow up with infra to reduce batch job priority and schedule a capacity bump proposal. I'll also coordinate a quiet maintenance window with Lina/account.
Lina: I'll coordinate the customer communication and request a short SLA credit if they want — will update thread.
Maya: final notes: incident severity lowered to SEV-2 since customer-approved in-VPC pin removed hosting risk. We'll keep monitoring for 2h then re-evaluate rollback to default routing after capacity fixes. :hourglass:
Elliot: filing a short incident summary to support ops and tagging customer thread.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: ospreybank-prod mitigated (model_pin applied). Notes: follow-up: postmortem due 72h. Paging cleared. :white_check_mark:
